bet.text: In an off-season interview: the collector follows "we touch it we keep it": very wide, flexible in both directions, meant to take in any ball the team can.

demand.text: When laying out the robot, the main thing the team wanted was the climber in the center, so the robot could be on whichever side of the hangar it needed.
Its championship partner 254 says the alliance wanted a triple traversal climb, for strategic flexibility and a higher points ceiling.

auto.text: A dashboard selector holds many tested autos, to fit what partners run. At the championship the team left 254's part of the field to 254 and ran its own two-ball.
A host's recap says that in the first Einstein final it scored two in the upper hub, then pushed an opposing ball to the hidden side of the hub.

cycle.text: In an off-season interview: wheels push cargo to an off-center tunnel, where beam breaks help tell its color; the wrong color goes out the back. Belts running in opposite directions hold a ball. An indicator turns blue with two balls; on the prime button the drivetrain faces the hub, the Limelight corrects, and it turns red.

endgame.text: In an off-season interview: pneumatics raise the climber until it latches. It climbs to the second bar, shifts the center of gravity to lift to the third, shifts again on the traversal and releases, all automated. The fastest climb was about nine seconds.

gave_up.text: A centered climber led to an off-center shooter and a center of gravity problem. To balance the robot the team belted and shafted three gearboxes and the flywheel over to the other side.
A host's recap says that in one qualification match the robot fell off the traversal rung with five seconds left.

changed.text: In an off-season interview: the shooter did not start with back rollers or a ball stopper. The rollers keep two balls at the same speed; the stopper, added between the regionals as a team member believes, keeps balls from coming out early. About halfway the team found latching that avoided two claws on each side.

outcome.text: 55-3-1 in official play; won the Galileo division, won the championship; captain of the Galileo alliance on Einstein; ranked 17 of the pooled top 20 (OPR 57.03, Galileo).
